why: The update is the documented logit-space rule; both the sync store (record -> _recompute) and the SQL store (record -> recompute, sweep) call update_rule, so repeated full-strength observations add ln(LR) per row and saturate toward 1.0 (the boundary guards return 0/1). Executed: `pytest tests/eval/test_evidence_invariants.py -q` -> 56 passed with the `engine-#83` parameter live (the E1 file is unchanged by this commit); TestConfidenceRange drives 50 observations monotonically. Supplied live measurement (not run by me): first user_confirm = 0.9523809523809523, second sensor = 0.9950248756218905.

The SQL recompute skips rows older than now - window; window = WINDOW[mutability] is EPHEMERAL 1d / MUTABLE 182d / SEMI_STATIC 1825d. sweep iterates every non-static fact that has evidence and calls recompute with a fresh UTC now, so stored confidence returns to the posterior after expiry; the row is retained (no DELETE). Executed: E1 TestEvidenceWindowExpiry (56 passed); tests/memory/test_evidence_store.py expiry and boundary tests (58 passed). Supplied live measurement (not run by me): ephemeral 0.9090909090909091 -> 0.5 after sweep at +1d1h.

Evidence is value-tagged with sha256(symbolic_repr); recompute skips rows whose value_hash differs from the current value, so a value change deactivates old evidence and the posterior returns to 0.5; evidence rows are not deleted, so reverting reactivates them. Executed: E1 TestValueHashMatching (56 passed); SQL test_recompute_ignores_evidence_for_another_value (58 passed). Supplied live measurement (not run by me): value change -> 0.5, revert -> 0.9950248756218905. Advisory: the FactStore integration test simulates the value change by writing repo.facts[id].symbolic_repr directly; FactStore.add_fact dedups on symbolic_repr and PostgresFactRepository.update does not accept symbolic_repr, so there is no production in-place value-change path yet. The engine law itself is implemented and tested.

The SQL dedup SELECT uses the same key and the inclusive observed_at >= cutoff boundary, and returns None before the insert; the sync store has the same loop. Executed: E1 TestDedup (duplicate within hour, exactly +1h, after window, key composition) -> 56 passed; SQL test_duplicate_within_the_inclusive_hour_is_discarded -> 58 passed. Supplied live measurement (not run by me): duplicate at +30m and exactly +1h discarded. Advisory: dedup is a SELECT-then-INSERT outside a transaction and the migration has no unique constraint, so two concurrent identical observations can both insert. The E1 contract does not require concurrency safety; the sequential window is correct. The predicate also has no upper bound, so a future-dated row suppresses a new observation until future+1h; that is exactly the E1 contract's documented `observed_at >= now - 1h` rule (the reference has no upper bound either), so it is contract-consistent, but clock-skew/future timestamps are a residual risk.

New static facts are stored at 1.0 (FactStore static branch) and record pins/returns None without touching the evidence table; recompute also pins static facts to 1.0. Retraction is refused before repo.retract, and ContextProvider.retract_fact only cascades when the FactStore reports success, so a refused static retraction cannot invalidate concepts. Executed: E1 TestStaticFacts (56 passed); test_fact_store_evidence.py::TestStaticFacts (58 passed). Supplied live measurement (not run by me): static 1.0 with 0 evidence. Advisory: the generic FactStore.update_fact still passes a caller-supplied confidence to repo.update; no caller uses it today, but it is an unguarded pin bypass.

The new-fact path saves at PRIOR, sets the in-memory stored.confidence to the incoming confidence (the observation strength), and calls record; the store inserts that strength and recomputes from PRIOR, so the first observation uses the same update rule as later ones. Executed: test_fact_store_evidence.py::TestNewFact (58 passed); E1 stored=posterior test starts from PRIOR (56 passed). Supplied live measurement (not run by me): first user_confirm 0.9523809523809523 = sigmoid(logit(0.5)+ln 20). A brand-new fact id has no evidence rows, so record cannot dedup and the only None cases are static (handled before) and no observation (always supplied); if record raises, the row stays at PRIOR and the next write records evidence and self-heals.

No retrieval file changed: git show --stat 8e8c028 touches src/cortex/memory/{evidence_store,fact_store,conversation_extractor}.py, src/cortex/main.py, src/cortex/services/minion_service.py, migrations/010_evidence.sql, tests and docs; it does not touch src/cortex/memory/repository.py or context_provider.py. why: recompute starts from PRIOR, applies only active rows in observed_at order, and writes the posterior with UPDATE facts SET confidence = $2; sweep calls it for every non-static fact that has evidence. Executed: E1 TestStoredConfidenceEqualsPosterior (56 passed); SQL recompute tests assert the written posterior (58 passed); full suite 1691 passed. Supplied live measurement (not run by me): 0.9090909090909091 -> 0.5 after sweep at +1d1h. Advisory: record commits the evidence insert and then recomputes in a second session; if the recompute fails or the process crashes, confidence is stale until the next hourly sweep (self-healing, not atomic). The refreshed row is the posterior after a successful recompute; a deduped duplicate returns the stored posterior without recomputing, which can be at most one sweep interval stale if older evidence expired in the meantime (the sweep is the repair path).

The module exports the required sync EvidenceStore (no-arg), update_rule, LR_BASE, PRIOR, DEDUP_WINDOW, WINDOW, Observation and Evidence; record/get_confidence/recompute/sweep/evidence_for match the seam. The E1 file is untouched by the commit and now runs unskipped: executed `pytest tests/eval/test_evidence_invariants.py -q` -> 56 passed (the engine-#83 parameter resolves, 27 engine nodes), versus the old importorskip. The full 1691-test canonical run had no skips.

PostgresEvidenceStore implements record (SQL dedup inclusive, insert, recompute at observed_at), recompute (value_hash+window from PRIOR), get_confidence (KeyError unknown), evidence_for (ORDER BY observed_at) and sweep (non-static facts with evidence); the session factory defaults to DbSession at call time and accepts an injected adapter. The SQL tests pin the same laws as E1: dedup boundary and params, insert strength, value-hash filter, expiry and boundary, static pin, written posterior, sweep query. FactStore integration: new fact stored at PRIOR, strength=incoming confidence, record -> recompute -> refresh; existing fact update omits confidence, record uses the incoming strength, and the refreshed DB row is returned; dedup returns the prior posterior; static pin/no evidence/retraction refusal; incoming STATIC over existing MUTABLE keeps existing mutability and is recorded as evidence (the test asserts <1.0, so it cannot pin); source mapping llm/conversation, sensor/events+minions; the no-evidence-store path is preserved.
